questions.question: What do you mean by physical spoilage of food? / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What do you mean by physical spoilage of food?
  • Physical spoilage refers to the deterioration of food caused by physical factors such as
  • mechanical damage, temperature fluctuations, moisture loss or gain, and improper handling
  • or storage.

questions.question: What is hydrogen swell? Discuss the factors favouring hydrogen swell? / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• What is hydrogen swell? Discuss the factors favouring hydrogen swell?
  • It is the bulging or swelling of canned foods caused by hydrogen gas produced inside the can
  • due to chemical reactions (usually between acids in food and the metal of the can).
  • Factors favouring hydrogen swell:
  • • High acidity of food
  • • High storage temperature
  • • Presence of dissolved oxygen
  • • Poor quality or damaged can lining
  • • Long storage time
  • • Presence of metal contaminants that speed up corrosion
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain fat soluble vitamins? / [CO1, CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain fat soluble vitamins?
  • Vitamins that dissolve in fats and oils, not in water.
  • • They are stored in the body's fatty tissues and liver.
  • • Include Vitamins A, D, E, and K.
  • • Absorption requires dietary fat.
  • Vitamin A
  • • Important for vision, immunity, and healthy skin.
  • • Found in liver, eggs, milk, and orange-coloured vegetables (carrots).
  • Vitamin D
  • • Helps in calcium absorption and bone health.
  • • Produced in skin by sunlight; also in fish, egg yolk, fortified foods.
  • Vitamin E
  • • Acts as an antioxidant that protects cells from damage.
  • • Found in nuts, seeds, and vegetable oils.
  • Vitamin K
  • • Essential for blood clotting and bone metabolism.
  • • Found in green leafy vegetables (spinach, kale).
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Write a note on the effect of temperature on storage of harvested products? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write a note on the effect of temperature on storage of harvested products/
  • • Respiration rate is decreased.
  • • Water loss is reduced.
  • • Ethylene production is suppressed.
  • • Sensitivity to ethylene is reduced.
  • • Microbial development is slowed.

questions.question: What are the importance of functional foods? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What is the importance of functional foods?
  • • Convenience: Functional foods offer a convenient way to incorporate health-
  • promoting ingredients into your diet.
  • • Targeted benefits: They can provide specific health benefits, such as supporting
  • heart health or digestive health.
  • • Increased nutrition: Functional foods can enhance the nutritional value of your
  • diet.
  • • Supports overall health: They can help prevent or manage chronic diseases, like
  • osteoporosis or diabetes.
  • • Wide availability: Functional foods are widely available in stores and online.

questions.question: Whic are the common challenges that occur while transporting harvested products? / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Which are the common challenges that occur while transporting harvested products?
  • • Damage: Rough handling, improper packaging, or long transit times can lead
  • to bruising, crushing, or contamination of harvested products.
  • • Spoilage: If temperature or humidity is not adequately controlled, the products
  • may spoil during transit, resulting in financial loss and waste.
  • • Delays: Transportation delays, due to factors like traffic, weather, or customs
  • procedures, can lead to the deterioration of perishable goods.
  • • Cost: Transporting perishable items, especially over long distances, can be
  • costly due to the need for refrigerated containers, quicker transportation
  • methods, and careful handling.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define concentration and explain its types? / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Define concentration and explain its types?
  • Concentration is a food preservation process in which a part of the water is removed
  • from a liquid food (like juices, milk, soups) to increase the solids content and reduce
  • volume.

• Differentiate between prebiotics and probiotics?
  • Prebiotics are non-digestible fibres or carbohydrates that feed the good bacteria in the gut,
  • promoting their growth and activity.
  • Probiotics are defined as: “Live microorganisms that, when administered in adequate
  • amounts, confer a health benefit on the host."

questions.question: Explain irradation, types of rays, its advantages and disadvantages? / [CO2, CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain irradiation, types of rays, its advantages and disadvantages?
  • Irradiation:
  • • A food preservation method where food is exposed to ionizing radiation to kill
  • microorganisms, insects, and delay spoilage.
  • Types of rays used:
  • • Gamma rays
  • • X-rays
  • • Electron beams (e-beams)
  • Advantages:
  • • Kills microbes and insects
  • • Extends shelf life
  • • Delays ripening and sprouting
  • • Maintains nutritional quality
  • Disadvantages:
  • • Requires expensive equipment
  • • Cannot kill all viruses/toxins
  • • Some consumers fear the process
  • • Not suitable for all foods (e.g., high-fat foods may get off-flavours)
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Define food and explain its classification? / [CO1, CO2] [15x1 = 15]
questions.solution_html:
• Define food and explain its classification?
  • Food is defined as anything solid or liquid which when swallowed, digested, and
  • assimilated, nourishes the body.
  • Classification
  • • Based on origin- plant and animal origin
  • • Based on functions- Physiological functions of food, Psychological functions of
  • food, Social function of food.
  • • Based on nutrients- micro and macro nutrients
  • • Based on pH- low acid foods, medium acid foods, acid foods, highly acid foods
